sampling_model.design: \(K\) independent randomized encouragement trials, source block \(s\) containing \(n_s\) i.i.d. observations, with externally fixed target composition.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary encouragement has known \(e_s(x)\); receipt and outcome satisfy consistency, exclusion, and monotonicity.
sampling_model.overlap: \(0<p_0\le1\), \(p_s(x)\ge p_0\) on \(\mathcal H_s\), randomized-arm overlap holds, and \(\operatorname{supp}(p_T)\subseteq\bigcup_s\mathcal H_s\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-cell frequencies, arm means, and residual variances are empirical. A deterministic floor and bounded fallback make profiling total; no unique oracle optimizer is required.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 identifies target potential-outcome means under conditions A1--A5; Theorem 2 uses weaker collection-level positivity; Theorem 3 uses cell-specific trial subsets and union support; and Theorem 4 identifies an average treatment effect under exchangeability in effect measure.
Equation (4) identifies a single-source transported CACE whose denominator is the instrument-to-receipt contrast in the target site, and Result 3 gives its efficient influence curve.
Theorem 3.2 establishes uniformly correct asymptotic size for an orthogonalized Anderson--Rubin LATE test.
Lemma 2 derives the efficient influence function and optimal source weights for a regular multi-source target average treatment effect.
The paper constructs weak-IV-robust inverted confidence sets and analyzes expected arc length in an invariant circular model.
Theorems 1--3 use ordered moduli to bound and construct honest confidence intervals for linear functionals over nested classes.
The paper identifies and regularly estimates a target-population CACE from a single study.

body.tldr: A transported complier effect is identified when target cells are covered only by the union of randomized encouragement trials, but honest precision depends on where residual precision lies in the support hypergraph. The collection index \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}=\mu_D^2/V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)\) uses the value of a constrained source-cell variance program, and \(1/V_{\mathrm{coll}}\) is the exact information in the labeled pooled observed-data experiment. A fully empirical profiled Anderson--Rubin inversion is uniformly honest and attains expected length of order \(\min\{1,T_{\mathrm{coll}}^{-1/2}\}\); a support-preserving continuum supplies the all-procedure lower bound. Two matched four-source collections have different values solely because precision is paired with support differently, proving that collection-only geometry is not a support-retaining single-source or Kish-style scalar reduction.

project_justification.gap: Dahabreh et al., Theorems 1--4, identify transported potential-outcome means or average effects under several exchangeability and positivity regimes; Section 3.4.2 and Theorem 3 provide the precise cell-specific trial-subset and union-support logic. Weak-IV theory establishes honest inversion for single moment systems. Neither literature characterizes honest confidence length for a transported noncompliance ratio assembled over a source-support hypergraph.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the observed-law information modulus for a bounded causal ratio under simultaneous weak compliance and union-only trial support.
project_justification.fill: The collection quadratic program is derived as the attainable score variance and the least-favorable testing modulus; an empirical profiled inversion and a continuum lower experiment give matching length rates, while a strict-separation construction proves the program cannot be collapsed to marginal scalar summaries.

body.related_work: Dahabreh et al. (2023), Theorem 1, identify target potential-outcome means under conditions A1--A5. Their Theorem 2 weakens treatment and participation positivity to the pooled collection conditions A3* and A5*. Section 3.4.2 defines the covariate-specific covering-trial set, and Theorem 3 combines the corresponding exchangeability condition A4\(^{\dagger}\) with union-support condition A5\(^{\dagger}\); this is the precise workflow grounding for collection-only support here. Their Theorem 4 instead identifies an average treatment effect under exchangeability in effect measure A4\(^{\ddagger}\). None of Theorems 1--4 contains a noncompliance ratio, a null-dependent source allocation, or weak-identification length theory. Rudolph and van der Laan (2017), equation (4) and Result 3, identify and efficiently estimate a single-source transported CACE in the five-site Moving to Opportunity application; their denominator uses instrument-to-receipt behavior observed in the target site, whereas the novel compliance-ITT transport condition here reconstructs the target first stage from covering source trials. Su et al. (2024), Lemma 2, optimize source weights for a regular nonratio target effect. Ma (2026), Algorithm 2.1 and Theorem 3.2, supplies the orthogonal Anderson--Rubin principle for LATE; the all-null score-price nondegeneracy here is a novel paper condition and is not attributed to Ma. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016) treat a null-indexed functional nuisance. Mikusheva (2010) is conceptual precedent for weak-IV strength indexing and robust confidence-set geometry, but does not define \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}\) or the collection strength floor. Cai and Low (2004) give ordered-modulus expected-length tools. These results inform the construction; no strict extension of their model-specific theorems is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The target composition \(p_T\) is externally fixed. A random target sample for a superpopulation estimand contributes an additional target-composition influence term to \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}\). The finite-cell model also excludes high-dimensional nuisance learning.
body.honest_scope: Identification, exact pooled-information equivalence, non-subsumption by support-retaining single-source geometry, uniform coverage, matching expected-length rate, strict collection separation, regular efficiency, and membership of the explicit least-favorable families are to be proved. The \(K=1\) result is only an algebraic sanity check. The exact minimax constant remains open. The compliance-ITT transport restriction and the collection-strength class are novel paper conditions; the former replaces target-site receipt data with protocol-invariant first-stage transport across covering sources, and the latter indexes compliance relative to exact collection information. Mikusheva provides only conceptual weak-IV precedent for the latter. The novel variance assumption is the cell-and-score lower bound \(\inf_{\theta}q_{sx}(\theta)\ge v_0\), weaker than armwise lower bounds and used only to keep studentization uniform over the inverted nulls; bounded data and propensity overlap supply its upper counterpart. The class explicitly requires \(0<p_0\le1\), which admits both singleton-support constructions because their supported-cell masses equal one.
